rationale: The item asks whether fear has led the respondent to put off making a dental appointment, which is the concept OHD_0005012 (delay in scheduling a dental appointment); this satisfies the axiom of OHD_0008024, the most specific class on its branch, so its ancestors (dental visit avoidance, health encounter avoidance, avoidance behavior, avoidance/anticipatory fear) are omitted, and 'prior to dental visit' is not inferred because dental visit avoidance behavior is only stated to 'precede only' a dental visit, not 'precede some' as OHD_0008037 requires.

The item asks whether fear has caused the respondent to cancel or not appear for a dental appointment, which is the concept OHD_0005013 (dental visit avoidance behavior that involves canceling or not showing up for a dental appointment); this satisfies OHD_0008023, the most specific class on the avoidance branch, so its ancestors (dental visit, health encounter and avoidance behavior questions, and the avoidance or anticipatory fear question) are omitted, and 'prior to dental visit' is not entailed because avoidance behavior only 'precedes only' a dental visit.

The item asks about muscle tension, i.e., EMRO_0000010 muscle tension response to emotion, which is a muscle contraction (GO_0006936) under muscle system process and therefore a GO_0003008 system process; this satisfies the axiom for OHD_0008047 question about physiological arousal, and no more specific child class covers muscle tension.

The item asks about an increased breathing rate (EMRO_0000012), which is a respiratory system process and therefore a GO_0003008 system process, so it satisfies the axiom for 'question about physiological arousal' (OHD_0008047), which has no more specific subclass that fits.

Perspiring is sweat secretion in response to emotion (EMRO_0000008), which is a subclass of sweat secretion and therefore of secretion by tissue (GO_0032941), so the item satisfies the definition of question about physiological arousal (OHD_0008047).

The item asks about feeling nauseated, which matches the concept nausea (OHD_0008051), a subclass of pathological bodily process (OGMS_0000061), so it satisfies the 'is about some pathological bodily process' disjunct of the physiological arousal question axiom (OHD_0008047); no more specific child class applies.

The item asks about an increased heart rate, which is the concept EMRO_0000011 (increased heart response to emotion); this is a heart process, a circulatory system process, and therefore a GO_0003008 system process, so the item satisfies the definition of OHD_0008047 (question about physiological arousal), and no more specific class exists for heart rate.

This Dental Fear Survey item asks about fear felt while making a dental appointment, which is a process before a dental visit (OHD_0008037), so it satisfies 'question about prior to dental visit'; it is also listed in the DFS avoidance/anticipatory fear subscale, and it does not describe actually delaying or cancelling an appointment, so the avoidance behavior classes do not apply.

Approaching the dentist's office is a process that precedes a dental visit, so the item is about OHD_0008037 and satisfies 'question about prior to dental visit' (OHD_0008041); it is also a DFS item on the fixed item list of the avoidance/anticipatory fear subscale (OHD_0008007), as I recall that subscale's item list.

The item asks about the patient sitting in a waiting room (OHD_0008027), which satisfies 'question about patient sitting in a waiting room' (OHD_0008029); its parent 'question about during dental visit' is omitted as an ancestor, and the DFS subscale classes are not assigned because their item lists are not given.

Being seated in the dental chair is a sitting process (OHD_0008038) that happens during a dental visit while the patient's role is being realized, so it counts as a process during a dental visit (OHD_0008039); no narrower existing class fits (the waiting-room class concerns a different setting), so it maps to 'question about during dental visit', and it is also included under the item-list-defined 'avoidance or anticipatory fear question' on the assumption that this DFS item belongs to the avoidance/anticipatory fear subscale, which the ontology's item list itself does not confirm.

This item asks about fear of the dental office smell and corresponds to DFS item 12. In the standard DFS factor structure, item 12 belongs to the avoidance/anticipatory fear subscale (items 1, 2, 8–12, 20), whose membership is fixed by item list; no Part 2 concept (smell or olfactory perception) is stated in the ontology, so no content-based class such as 'during dental visit' can be inferred.

'Seeing the dentist walk in' is DFS item 14, which belongs to the avoidance/anticipatory fear subscale (OHD_0008007, defined by its item list), and it describes a process in which the patient takes part during a dental visit (OHD_0008039), so it also satisfies question about during dental visit (OHD_0008042); no more specific dental procedure or waiting room class applies.

'Seeing the anesthetic needle' is Dental Fear Survey item 14, which belongs to the fixed DFS list for fear of specific dental stimuli (OHD_0008046); it also describes something the patient experiences in the patient role during a dental visit, so it satisfies 'process during dental visit' and therefore OHD_0008042, while no Part 2 concept for injection or needle supports a more specific dental procedure class.

This item is the Dental Fear Survey item 'Feeling the needle injected', which belongs to the DFS fear-of-specific-dental-stimuli subscale (OHD_0008046); a dental injection is a process realizing the dental provider and dental patient roles, so it is a dental procedure (OHD_0000002), which makes the item a dental procedure question (OHD_0008044), the most specific class on the during-dental-visit branch.

'Seeing the drill' is a Dental Fear Survey item that measures fear evoked by a specific dental stimulus, the drill, so it belongs to the fixed DFS item list for fear of specific dental stimuli (OHD_0008046). The item is also about the tooth drilling procedure (OHD_0008028), a subclass of dental procedure, so it satisfies the question about tooth drilling (OHD_0008030), which already covers its ancestors.

Hearing the drill is about the tooth drilling procedure (OHD_0008028), a subclass of dental procedure, so the item satisfies 'question about tooth drilling' (OHD_0008030); it is also the Dental Fear Survey item 'Hearing the drill', which I am assuming from general knowledge of the DFS belongs to the fear-of-specific-dental-stimuli subscale (OHD_0008046), since the ontology text does not list that subscale's items.

The item asks about the sensation of the drill during a tooth drilling procedure (OHD_0008028, a dental procedure), so it satisfies 'question about tooth drilling'; it is also, I believe, one of the Dental Fear Survey drill items that make up the fixed 'fear of specific dental stimuli' subscale, which sits on a separate branch.

The item asks about undergoing a tooth cleaning procedure (OHD_0008034), which is a dental procedure, so it satisfies 'question about a tooth cleaning procedure' (OHD_0008035), the most specific class on the during-visit/dental procedure branch; the DFS-list-defined 'fear of specific dental stimuli' class was not chosen because its item list is not given.

The item asks about overall fear of having dental work done. Dental work is a dental procedure (OHD_0000002), so the item meets the axiom for dental procedure question (OHD_0008044). Its focus on fear of undergoing a procedure also matches the text definition of fear of medical procedure question (OHD_0008054), which sits on a separate branch, so both classes are kept.

The item asks about anxiety felt shortly before going to the dentist, which is a process before dental visit (OHD_0008037); that satisfies the axiom for question about prior to dental visit (OHD_0008041). It is not a Dental Fear Survey item, so the list-defined avoidance or anticipatory fear class does not apply, and no avoidance behavior or physiological arousal is described.

The item asks about generally avoiding going to the dentist because of distress, which is dental visit avoidance behavior (OHD_0005007); it does not specify canceling, no-shows or delayed scheduling, so the most specific matching class is dental visit avoidance question (OHD_0008022), and its ancestors are dropped.

The item measures anticipatory nervousness about upcoming dental visits, which is a process before a dental visit (OHD_0008037, which precedes some dental visit), so it satisfies 'question about prior to dental visit'; it is not a listed DFS item for the anticipatory-fear subscale, and 'nervous or edgy' is not stated in the ontology as a system process or secretion, so physiological arousal does not apply.

new_node.label: question about negative cognition regarding dental care
new_node.definition: A question that assesses an individual's negative or catastrophic thoughts or beliefs about dental visits or dental treatment, such as expecting that something harmful or bad will happen.
new_node.logical_definition: question AND (is about some negative cognition regarding dental care)

new_concept.label: negative cognition regarding dental care
new_concept.definition: A cognition in which an individual holds negative or catastrophic thoughts or beliefs about dental visits or dental treatment, such as expecting harm, danger, or a bad outcome.

rationale: The item asks about a catastrophic belief that something bad would happen when visiting a dentist, which is a cognition (GO_0050890). It is not avoidance behavior, a physiological arousal process, or a specific procedure or visit phase, and the anticipatory-fear class is a fixed DFS item list, so a new class about negative dental cognitions is proposed.

The item measures a general fear felt while visiting the dentist, which is a process in which the patient, realizing the dental patient role, participates during a dental visit (OHD_0008039 process during dental visit). It therefore satisfies 'question about during dental visit'. It names no specific procedure, pain, avoidance behavior or bodily arousal, so no more specific class applies, and the fear-related classes are either fixed DFS item lists or are about a medical procedure or pain rather than the visit itself.

The item measures an increased heart rate as an emotional response to dental care. That is EMRO_0000011 (increased heart response to emotion), which is a heart process, a circulatory system process and a GO_0003008 system process, so it satisfies the physiological arousal question axiom. 'When I go to the dentist' could mean on the way or at the visit, so it does not clearly assert a process during the dental visit.

The item asks about delaying making dentist appointments, which is the concept 'dental visit avoidance behavior that involves delay in scheduling a dental appointment' (OHD_0005012); by its equivalence axiom this satisfies 'question about delay in scheduling a dental appointment' (OHD_0008024), the most specific class on the avoidance branch, while 'prior to dental visit' is excluded because the 'precedes only' axiom does not make the behavior a process before dental visit, and the list-based DFS subscale classes are excluded because this item is not on the DFS list.

The item asks about anticipatory worry before going to the dentist, which is a process before a dental visit (OHD_0008037) and so satisfies 'question about prior to dental visit' (OHD_0008041); the avoidance or anticipatory fear class is excluded because its membership is a fixed list of DFS items, not set by content.

The item asks whether going to the dentist is actively avoided. This is dental visit avoidance behavior (OHD_0005007), which satisfies the dental visit avoidance question (OHD_0008022). The item does not specify canceling, not showing up, or delaying scheduling, so no more specific subclass applies, and the 'endured with intense fear' clause matches no stated concept-based class.

new_node.label: question about duration of dental fear
new_node.definition: A question that assesses how long an individual's fear or anxiety about dental care or dental visits has persisted, such as whether it has been present for a minimum period of time.
new_node.logical_definition: question AND (is about some persistent dental fear)

new_concept.label: persistent dental fear
new_concept.definition: An unpleasant emotional experience of fear or anxiety directed at dental care or dental visits that persists over an extended period of time (e.g., at least 6 months).

rationale: The item measures how long the person's fear of going to the dentist has lasted (at least 6 months), not a specific avoidance behavior, visit phase, procedure, stimulus or bodily arousal; the DFS-list classes exclude non-DFS items, so a new class about persistent dental fear, an emotional experience, is proposed.

The item asks whether one's avoidance of going to the dentist (OHD_0005007, dental visit avoidance behavior, which makes it a dental visit avoidance question, OHD_0008022) affects one's life, and it names being embarrassed about the appearance of the teeth (EMRO_0003002, which makes it a question about embarrassment, OHD_0008085) as one of those effects; these are unrelated branches, so both of their most specific classes are kept.

The item measures fear of a panic attack, which it describes by its physiological arousal symptoms: sweating (sweat secretion response to emotion, a secretion by tissue) and pounding heart (increased heart response to emotion, a system process); this satisfies the axiom of question about physiological arousal, while the DFS-list-defined classes and the visit-timing classes are not clearly met.

The item attributes dental fear to self-consciousness and concern about being watched or judged by others, which matches the Part 2 concept embarrassment (a self-conscious emotional experience involving the attention or observation of others), so it satisfies question about embarrassment, the most specific class on its branch (it subsumes its ancestor, question about physiological arousal, via cognition being a nervous system process).

The item asks how anxious the respondent is about undergoing painful or uncomfortable procedures at the dentist. Because it is about a dental procedure (OHD_0000002), it satisfies the dental procedure question axiom, which is more specific than 'question about during dental visit'. Its content also matches the text definitions of 'fear of medical procedure question' (fear of undergoing a procedure) and 'fear of pain question' (fear of painful procedures); neither class has logical axioms, so both are assigned on their text definitions. One caveat: their shared parent, OHD_0008007, is defined by a fixed DFS item list rather than by content, so if this item is not on that list, the two fear classes may be disputed.

The item measures anxiety about feeling embarrassed or ashamed at the dentist, so it is about embarrassment [EMRO_0003002] and satisfies 'question about embarrassment' [OHD_0008085]; the ontology does not state that embarrassment realizes a dental patient role, so 'question about during dental visit' cannot be inferred.

The item asks about anxiety over not being in control of what happens while the patient is at the dentist, which is a process during the dental visit in which the patient takes part; no more specific procedure, waiting-room, avoidance or embarrassment class applies, so it maps to 'question about during dental visit' (OHD_0008042) via 'process during dental visit' (OHD_0008039).

The item asks about feeling sick or queasy, which matches the concept nausea [OHD_0008051]; nausea is a pathological bodily process [OGMS_0000061], so the item satisfies the axiom for question about physiological arousal [OHD_0008047]; the ontology does not state that nausea happens during a dental visit, so 'during dental visit' is not inferred.

The item asks how anxious the patient is about numbness from the anesthetic when visiting the dentist, which is a process the patient experiences in the dental patient role during a dental visit (OHD_0008039), so it fits 'question about during dental visit'; it is not a listed DFS item, and numbness is not one of the arousal concepts given, so the physiological arousal class is not justified.

new_node.label: question about uncertainty regarding a dental procedure
new_node.definition: A question that is about a patient's lack of knowledge or uncertainty about what dental procedure will be performed or what will happen during a dental visit.
new_node.logical_definition: question AND (is about some uncertainty about dental procedure)

new_concept.label: uncertainty about dental procedure
new_concept.definition: A phenomenal cognitive experience during a dental visit in which a patient is aware of lacking knowledge about what dental procedure the dental health care provider is going to perform.

rationale: The item measures anxiety, while at the dentist, about the unknown nature of what the dentist will do, so it is about a dental procedure (a process during a dental visit) and maps to dental procedure question (OHD_0008044); no existing class captures the core construct of uncertainty or lack of information, so a reusable child class is proposed for this and similar items.

new_node.label: question about cost of dental treatment
new_node.definition: A question that is about the financial cost of, or payment for, dental treatment.
new_node.logical_definition: question AND (is about some payment for dental treatment)

new_concept.label: payment for dental treatment
new_concept.definition: A planned process in which a patient or a third party pays the financial cost of dental treatment provided by a dental health care provider.

rationale: The item asks about anxiety over the financial cost of dental treatment, which is not a dental procedure, avoidance behavior, physiological arousal, waiting-room process, or defined before/during/after-visit process, so no existing class fits and a new cost-of-treatment question class is proposed.

new_node.label: question about dental injection
new_node.definition: A question that is about some injection procedure performed on a patient during a dental visit, such as an injection of local anesthetic.
new_node.logical_definition: [OHD_0008044] dental procedure question AND (is about some dental injection procedure)

new_concept.label: dental injection procedure
new_concept.definition: A dental procedure in which a needle is used to inject a substance, such as a local anesthetic, into the oral tissues of a patient.

rationale: The item asks about anxiety over needles or injections received at the dentist, which is a dental procedure (OHD_0000002), so it satisfies dental procedure question (OHD_0008044); no injection-specific subclass exists alongside the drilling and cleaning ones, so a dental-injection subclass is proposed; the DFS-list-defined classes (OHD_0008046, and OHD_0008054 under OHD_0008007) are excluded because this is not a listed DFS item.

new_node.label: question about gagging or choking
new_node.definition: A question that is about an individual's experience of, or fear of, gagging or choking, for example during dental treatment.
new_node.logical_definition: question AND (is about some gagging or choking)

new_concept.label: gagging or choking
new_concept.definition: A pathological bodily process in which the throat contracts reflexively (gagging) or the airway is obstructed or felt to be obstructed (choking), commonly triggered by stimulation of the mouth or throat.

rationale: The item asks about anxiety over gagging or choking that happens while at the dentist, which places it under 'question about during dental visit' (OHD_0008039); because no existing concept captures gagging or choking (nausea is the only pathological bodily process listed), a new concept 'gagging or choking' under pathological bodily process (OGMS_0000061) is proposed, with a matching question class under 'question about physiological arousal' (OHD_0008047).

The item asks about anxiety over how the dentist treats the patient (unsympathetic or unkind) when the patient goes to the dentist; this interaction happens during the dental visit and realizes the dental patient role, so it is a process during dental visit (OHD_0008039), which satisfies 'question about during dental visit' (OHD_0008042); no more specific existing class, such as dental procedure or waiting room, applies.

The item asks how the respondent would feel the day before an upcoming dental treatment visit, so it is about a process before a dental visit (OHD_0008037) and satisfies 'question about prior to dental visit'. 'Avoidance or anticipatory fear question' is excluded because its membership is a fixed DFS item list, not set by content.

The item asks how the respondent would feel while sitting in the waiting room waiting for treatment, which is about the concept patient sitting in waiting room (OHD_0008027); that satisfies question about patient sitting in a waiting room (OHD_0008029), the most specific class, which is a child of question about during dental visit.

The item asks how the respondent feels when about to have a tooth drilled, so it is about a tooth drilling procedure (OHD_0008028), which is a dental procedure; this satisfies 'question about tooth drilling' (OHD_0008030), the most specific class on that branch. The DFS-list classes (avoidance or anticipatory fear question, fear of specific dental stimuli question) are excluded because membership is fixed by item list, not by content.

The item asks about feelings toward an upcoming tooth scaling procedure and tooth polishing procedure, both subclasses of tooth cleaning procedure (a dental procedure), so it satisfies 'question about a tooth cleaning procedure' (OHD_0008035), the most specific class on the dental procedure / during dental visit branch; the anticipation happens at the visit rather than before it, and the DFS-only anticipatory fear class does not apply.

The item asks about feelings when about to undergo a local anaesthetic injection in the gum, which is a dental procedure (OHD_0000002); this satisfies dental procedure question (OHD_0008044), the most specific match because no injection-specific class exists, and that class also covers its ancestor, question about during dental visit, while the avoidance/anticipatory-fear branch is excluded because its membership is limited to a fixed list of DFS items.
